findings.text: The generic guest address walker resolves a guest address to a host frame identifier while accumulating guest permissions, handling nested translation of both intermediate tables and the final mapping, and reporting a detailed fault record on failure. It supports retry when accessed or dirty tracking updates race with concurrent guest changes.

A guest entry is treated as terminal when a size indicator is present, with distinct handling for legacy 32-bit paging where the indicator is ignored at high levels without size support, whereas other paging modes treat the same indicator as either reserved or terminal. The smallest page size is always terminal.
Protection key information is only derived from guest entries under 64-bit paging; all other paging modes report no keys.

Updates to accessed and dirty tracking skip levels whose intermediate mapping was observed as unwritable and otherwise attempt an atomic user memory update, marking the underlying table dirty and refreshing cached entry state only after a successful update.

A walk starts from a root determined by current CPU mode, descends through levels with nested translation and visibility checks at each table, then validates terminal permissions and tracking state. Outcomes are success with a resolved frame, silent nested fault propagation, or a populated fault record with an error classification.

Permission state is accumulated across levels with execute control inverted so it can be combined uniformly, and fault classification merges write, user and fetch attributes with reserved and present indications plus guest versus nested stage information. Extended paging builds an additional violation qualification describing access kind, address validity and translation stage.
A thin wrapper invokes the generic walker using the current memory management unit configuration of the calling virtual CPU.

Prefetch of a guest entry is abandoned when the entry is deemed invalid for prefetch, otherwise the target frame and narrowed access derived from the shadow parent and guest protections are offered to the shadow prefetch helper after clean-entry write protection is applied.

Change detection rereads guest memory atomically and reports change when the read fails or the reread value differs from the cached walker value, using a batched read that also fills a prefetch cache for the smallest page size.

Neighbor entry prefetch is skipped for large-page parents and during address invalidation, and uses a separate direct-mapping path for direct parents. For shadow parents it scans a fixed-size aligned group around the faulting entry, ignoring the faulting slot itself and already present shadows, and stops at the first entry that cannot be prefetched.

Shadow construction first links indirect levels that mirror guest tables and then expands direct levels toward a target mapping size before installing the leaf. The process aborts with a retry request when guest state changed, when roots are invalid or placeholder, or when child synchronization needs to yield.

New indirect pages are synchronized before linkage and revalidated against current guest state while holding the mapping lock, with writes that target a shadowed table remembered in the fault state and with huge-page sizing deferred until after indirect resolution.

The shadow fault handler walks the guest tables without reserved-bit influence, injects an emulated fault when the guest has no mapping, resolves backing storage, and on success builds shadow state. It returns retry, write-protected, spurious or completion indications rather than directly resuming the guest.

The fault handler acquires the virtual machine mapping lock in write mode only after guest walk and backing resolution complete, and holds it across page availability checks, staleness checks, shadow construction and fault completion.

When guest write protection is disabled, a supervisor write to a nominally read-only user mapping is treated as writable supervisor-only for shadow purposes, with execute permission removed when supervisor execution prevention is active, except for emulated device mappings.
The address of the first entry described by a smallest-page shadow page is the page base plus a quadrant-derived offset under 32-bit paging and simply the page base otherwise.

Guest virtual to guest physical translation returns either a fully composed physical address on walk success or an invalid sentinel on failure, optionally copying the detailed fault record to caller storage.

Leaf synchronization reconciles one shadow entry with the current guest entry, handling device mappings, permission narrowing and entry removal, and reports distinct outcomes for unchanged or device-handled, changed or dropped, and unreadable cases.

Synchronization preserves the existing host frame and host writability while recomputing shadow access as a subset of prior access, drops the entry when the frame changes or no effective present state remains, and leaves the entry untouched when recomputed access is identical.

The walker carries current and maximum traversal levels, per-level cached entries with access summaries, per-level table identifiers and addresses, user pointers with writability observations, a resolved frame, a fault record and a small prefetch cache.

Fault handling uses a fault record with address, frame, slot, permission and sizing attributes plus flags for write, user, prefetch, device and shadow-table targeting, while shadow pages expose level, access, directness and quadrant attributes.

Guest table memory is read through host mappings that can fault, become invisible or change concurrently, so callers must handle retry, placeholder roots and invalidation races rather than assuming a single walk remains valid.
Device emulation caching is enabled by default through a frequently read shared flag, with a separate initialization-time flag controlling whether such caching is permitted.

Accessed and dirty support and all shadow entry bit selections are held in frequently read shared globals, including host and management writability, execute and user controls with two mutually exclusive extended execute variants, tracking masks, device value and mask selections, present and encryption selections, and nonpresent or reserved groupings.
Log output from this compilation unit is prefixed with the module name.
A setter records the per-virtual-machine device shadow value used when constructing device entries.
